findings.passage: “Most Texans have already proven their citizenship when they got their driver’s license, but the feds have not allowed us to do this for voter registration. Senate Bill 16 will address that,” Hughes said Tuesday during a Senate floor debate on the bill.
findings.note: Quoted by Votebeat from the Senate floor debate on SB 16, which would require proof of citizenship to register to vote.

findings.passage: “So we’re talking about a relatively small group of people,” Hughes said.
findings.note: Quoted by Votebeat from the same SB 16 floor debate. In the story he says many Texans have already shown proof of citizenship when getting a driver's license and election officials can verify others, so the group needing to act is small.

findings.passage: “We know that one non-citizen voting in an election is a problem,” Hughes added. “That cancels out the vote of a citizen.”
findings.note: Quoted by a Tyler TV station (KLTV) when he filed SB 16, a bill requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote. The same story quotes him: “We are not waiting on Washington, we can fix this locally.”

findings.passage: “None of us can deny that we can and should always work toward a better election process — one that is safer and more accessible — and that’s what Senate Bill 1 does,” said state Sen. Bryan Hughes, the Mineola Republican who has authored each version of the legislation.
findings.note: Quoted by the Texas Tribune at the Senate committee hearing on SB 1 (2021). SB 1 as passed added ID-number requirements to mail ballot applications and carrier envelopes.

findings.passage: “The security measures in this bill are aimed not at the voters trying to cheat but at ballot harvesters, at folks trying to influence, trying to coerce, trying to steal votes, trying to mislead voters,” Hughes added.
findings.note: Quoted by the Texas Tribune at the SB 1 committee hearing, about the bill's rules for people who assist voters.

findings.passage: “DPS will issue you a state ID if you don’t have a driver’s license. And then the objectors said, yeah, but you’ve got to pay a fee for that. And that would be like a poll tax,” Hughes explained. “We said, you’re right. So we made that voter ID card free from the state. We removed every possible obstacle and still got opposition.”
findings.note: Quoted by KLTV after a Fifth Circuit ruling that reinstated SB 1's mail-ballot ID requirement (last four of a Social Security number or a government ID number). He describes the free state voter ID card for people with no driver's license.

findings.passage: “We’re talking about common sense reforms, easy to vote, hard to cheat,” said Hughes.
findings.note: Quoted by KLTV about SB 1 (2021), in the same story on the Fifth Circuit ruling restoring mail-ballot ID rules.
